The *Parittārammaṇattika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 23.31) is a canonical Abhidhamma text forming part of the *Paṭṭhāna* in the Pali Tipiṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. It examines the intersection of the triad concerning limited or minor mental objects (*parittārammaṇa-ttika*) with the fundamental triad of wholesomeness, unwholesomeness, and undetermined states (*kusalattika*) according to the conditional relations of the Abhidhamma matrix [Catalog; SuttaCentral].

The largest degrees of textual correspondence occur with *Sanidassanattika, Dassanenapahātabbadukādi* (Patthana 22.35; 7 matches, including segments §1.1–2.1), *Tika Kusalattika* (Patthana 5.2; 7 matches, aligning §1.1–3.1_0 with §89.1–92.1), and *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 7 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Significant textual alignment also connects it with other sections analyzing similar matrices, such as *Pītittika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 23.25), *Parittārammaṇattika, Hetuduka* (Patthana 16.37), and the standalone *Parittārammaṇattika* (Patthana 1.14) [DharmaNexus].
